units.function: Embedded-PostgreSQL HTTP tests for adopting or clearing terminal stale Issue execution/checkout locks, preserving live ownership and terminal status, releasing rightful ownership, and tenant-admin force release with audit evidence.
units.dependencyDirection: Supertest/Express -> Issue routes -> Issue/Run ownership services -> Drizzle/PostgreSQL Issues, Agents, Runs, relations, comments and activity log.
units.keyDataModels: Issue assignee, checkoutRunId, executionRunId/name key/lockedAt/status; Agent and current/failed/timed-out/live Runs with Issue context; board/Agent principal; force-release previous-owner receipt and activity event.
units.lifecycle: Acquire Issue checkout/execution owner -> owner Run terminates or remains live -> same assignee/current Run adopts terminal ownership or release clears it; competing live Run receives conflict with no side effects; board can force clear with previous-state receipt; reassigned checkout self-heals terminal orphan.
units.testAssessment: All 11 tests skipped in sandboxed and approved unsandboxed runs because embedded PostgreSQL was unavailable. Intended coverage spans failed/timed-out adoption, four non-in-progress status-preservation cases, rightful release, live-owner conflict, no false checkout activity, board/tenant authorization and orphan healing. Missing are concurrent CAS/fencing, distributed Connector leases, broader status/corruption matrices, crash atomicity, force-release policy/reason/notification and immutable audit verification.
units.designRationale: Prevent dead Runs from pinning an Issue forever without allowing a contender to steal a live execution, and provide an explicit operator escape hatch with attribution.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs vendor-neutral execution leases that survive Connector/node failure, safely transfer ownership, preserve Work state and keep an accountable human informed whenever ownership is overridden.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT terminal-owner adoption, live-owner conflict, state-preserving release, tenant concealment and previous-state receipts. Model ExecutionLease with monotonically increasing fencing token, expiry/heartbeat and Connector attestation; mutate via tenant-scoped CAS plus transactional outbox; require reason, role/risk policy and sometimes approval for force release; notify responsible human and append an immutable LeaseOverrideReceipt.
units.responsibilityConflict: A coarse board admin can force-release without a reason or approval and can clear a still-live checkout owner. Mutable activity attribution records who clicked but not why they were authorized, what execution/evidence was abandoned or whether the accountable human and Connector were notified.
evidence: git history: seven commits from f91a6e27c0feb7f92dcde981c9a741b869484e83 through b69b563aa88af811ad45e658b0d8778ccb2f373d recorded in the read ledger
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL distributed ownership gap for Company OS: Run IDs are ownership markers but no monotonic fencing/CAS concurrency proof is present. HIGH force-release authority gap: no mandatory reason, risk policy, approval or affected-party notification. HIGH transaction/audit gap: no crash-atomic proof across lease, Work and activity state. HIGH verification gap: all database/HTTP tests skipped. MEDIUM lifecycle gap: lease expiry/heartbeat and full terminal/corrupt status taxonomy are absent. POSITIVE: live-owner rejection, terminal-owner recovery, tenant 404 and actor/previous-state receipt address recurrent lock failures without blind deletion.
